mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening labor market conditions, reducing consumer demand and corporate profit margins, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST for two consecutive quarters signals a broad-based weakening in aggregate demand, which compresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
